scope: Read-only assessment of determinism, fault injection points, recovery oracles, transition coverage, limits, and concurrency tests. No code or SDD changes.
summary: ?109.3 names the correct acceptance themes and correctly avoids inferring response delivery after a complete Sync. It is not yet a deterministic, executable matrix: crash offsets, exact failure seams and expected state assertions, race schedules, and boundary values are left implicit. Resolve the findings before calling the catalog test contract implementation-ready.
strengths: Separates complete valid frames from partial/corrupt frames and treats a complete valid chain as authoritative after restart; tests do not guess whether the old HTTP response arrived.
Includes golden frame/CRC, canonical JSON, global generation order, legal/illegal transitions, size/frame caps, writes and Sync, process restart, multi-process append, and OS-specific gates.
Requires fail-closed behavior and explicitly says uncertain catalog durability must prevent DB/sidecar/key opens.

findings.title: Crash-boundary coverage is not pinned to deterministic byte offsets and recovery oracles
findings.evidence: ?109.3 says ?complete-frame crash boundaries? and ?Restart at every frame boundary? but does not say whether this means inter-record boundaries or crashes inside a frame. The frame in ?109.1 has distinct magic, length, payload, CRC, repeated length, trailer, file Sync, first-create parent Sync, and response boundaries.
findings.risk: Different implementations can claim coverage while testing different crash points; a partial header/payload/footer or a full frame before/after Sync may escape the matrix.
findings.recommendation: Enumerate a child-process crash hook after each write component and before/after file Sync, parent Sync, and response. For each point specify expected bytes on disk, restart verdict (accept complete valid chain vs global integrity failure), state/generation, and whether case files may be opened. Use fixed payloads and case IDs for these tests.

findings.title: Fault-injection seams and per-failure assertions are underspecified
findings.evidence: ?109.3 names short write, partial frame, file Sync failure, and first-create parent Sync failure, but gives no injection contract or expected result per seam. The protocol also depends on lock acquisition, seek/read, exclusive create, full-chain parse, file Sync, parent Sync, and restart replay.
findings.risk: A generic injected error may never distinguish zero-byte write from partial/full-frame write with uncertain Sync; tests may verify only an error return while missing global poison, no retry, or forbidden DB/sidecar/key opens.
findings.recommendation: Define injectable operations (CreateExclusive, Lock, Seek, Read, Write(n,err), FileSync, ParentSync) and a case table with each failure point, prior durable state, returned class, poison scope, retry policy, restart result, and expected counts of DB/sidecar/key opens. Include short-write with n=0, 0<n<len, and full frame plus Sync error.

findings.title: Transition and capacity requirements lack explicit boundary vectors
findings.evidence: ?109.3 says to cover every allowed/forbidden transition and the size/frame-count limits, while ?109.2 has 11 allowed edges plus the absent initial state and many forbidden edges. ?109.1 defines 1?256-byte payloads, 16 MiB and 65,536-frame maxima, contiguous generations, and overflow failure.
findings.risk: ?Every? and ?limits? are hard to audit without a traceable vector list; off-by-one behavior, generation overflow, no-write-on-rejection, and accidental case-local rather than global generation checks can remain untested.
findings.recommendation: Add a transition table test with one positive and one negative vector for each source/destination pair, asserting record count/generation unchanged on rejection. Add exact max and max+1 vectors for payload length, total catalog bytes, frame count, and generation overflow; assert accepted maxima replay and rejected additions do not append or acknowledge.

findings.title: Cross-process race test has no deterministic scheduler or broader concurrency oracle
findings.evidence: ?109.3 asks two processes appending different cases to produce one contiguous generation chain, but does not define synchronization barriers, competing operations, or assertions for duplicate IDs, same-case state races, readers observing append in progress, or one process failing while holding/releasing the lock.
findings.risk: A timing/sleep-based test can pass without overlapping critical sections and may be flaky across Windows/POSIX or CI load.
findings.recommendation: Use named barriers/channels to force both children to contend at the lock boundary, then release in controlled orders. Assert exactly one contiguous global generation sequence, valid complete frames, legal per-case chains, no duplicate generation, no partial snapshot, and deterministic fail-closed/recovery behavior when a process exits at each lock/append phase. Run the same vectors on Windows and POSIX.

reviewed_areas.golden_wire_format: PARTIAL: required, but test fixture determinism and exact vector list should be stated
reviewed_areas.canonical_json_and_crc: PARTIAL: broad categories named; malformed cases and boundary vectors are not enumerated here
reviewed_areas.state_transitions: GAP: ?every? transition lacks a traceable matrix
reviewed_areas.crash_recovery: GAP: frame-internal crash offsets and expected recovery outcomes are not explicit
reviewed_areas.cross_process_concurrency: GAP: deterministic contention schedule and full oracle are absent
reviewed_areas.platform_security_gates: ACKNOWLEDGED_SEPARATELY: Windows/POSIX verified handle and ACL gates are explicitly reserved

exit_criteria: Add traceable deterministic vectors and explicit expected outcomes for every crash/failure injection point.
Add transition and numeric-boundary tables with no-write/no-ack assertions for rejected operations.
Specify barrier-controlled multi-process schedules and run them on both supported OS families.
